In GSI, this translates into a Bayesian network where each tier contributes a prior probability to the belief state. The truth rules define a precedence relation that resolves contradictions by temporal and authority-based dominance. For instance, when TIER 1 (official) contradicts TIER 2 (open data), the system must evaluate whether the official source is stale or genuinely updated. This induces a dualism in reasoning: one layer validates canonical truth while another ensures temporal coherence. The smoke-test example of Najee Harris and Rico Dowdle illustrates how discrepancies between rendered values and canonical truth trigger validation failures. The failure mode occurs when a stale or unverified source overrides a canonical truth without sufficient evidence. The system must detect such inconsistencies through telemetry and retroactively adjust belief states accordingly.
